newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures mixed, platinum group firmer.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures mixed, platinum group firmer.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo gold futures ended narrowly mixed on Thursday, while platinum group metals settled generally firmer as the yen's weaker tendency against the dollar provided support, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from two yen per gram lower to two yen firmer. Most-active benchmark December was two up at 1,349 yen.

In gold futures, private investors were tending to liquidate their longs in nearbys, while building fresh longs in distant months, backed by views that the dollar has more scope to rise against the yen, the traders said.
The dollar rose as high as 115.12 yen as of midday in Tokyo, its highest level in over 44 months.
In the bullion market, spot gold was trapped within tight ranges due to the Christmas holidays, quoted at $368.30/80 per ounce at the Tokyo close after opening at $368.50/369.00.
Platinum prices ended mostly at the day's highs as sporadic physical buying and fresh buying overwhelmed year-end long-liquidation, but activity was dull amid the holiday mood, the traders said.
The most-active benchmark December contract was up five yen per gram at 1,361 yen.

Japanese import data for November released by the ministry on Thursday showed gold imports were down by 56.3 percent year-on-year at 6.43 tonnes, while platinum imports were up 34.1 percent at 7.95 tonnes.
Traders said domestic gold demand led by the investment sector and jewellery sector remained sluggish, but platinum demand from the industrial sector and jewellery sector was relatively good,
Benchmark December palladium was up two yen per gram at 432 yen. Benchmark December silver was up 0.5 yen per 10 grams at 180.0 yen.-- K.Takagi, Tokyo Commodity Desk +81-3-3432-7431
